title: Java is not a 100 percent object-oriented language
answer: Java is not usually considered 100% object-oriented because primitive types such as `int`, `long`, `double`, `char`, and `boolean` are values rather than objects, and Java also supports static members associated with classes. At the same time, Java strongly supports OOP through classes, interfaces, inheritance, encapsulation, polymorphism, records, and object references. Wrapper classes such as `Integer` allow primitive values to participate in object-based APIs when necessary.
